First of all let me say that for this price and if you want to see the VH story concluded it is definitely a game worth buying! Don't listen to all the doomsayers...
Imho VH3 shows more improvements and changes than VH2 did. If that is for better or for worse is up to you to decide.
Features:
- 6 "new" classes: Those are pretty much the old 3 classes split down further. You have your ranged hunter, which is a class I simply can't really play so well anymore, because his main attack forces you to repeatedly press the left mouse button instead of simply holding it down like in the previous games. Why? Because if you hold it down you "charge" your shot. It's a cool feature, but something that should have been a secondary attack instead. Afaik there is no good skill to replace this with, because they all cost mana and the hunter does not have much mana...
Next is some sort of "tank" with a shield, then the classic mage, some sort of rogue, and engineer who relies on minions, which take up 50% of the screen estate, and my personal favorite, the Phlogistoneer, a mechanical exoskeleton with a flamethrower and missiles and a shield. That is my chosen class for now. It's fun and you're pretty well off with the first 2 skills. I didn't bother with anything else for now...doesn't seem worth it. My second pick would be the Mage, but he's a real glass cannon...
This, however, means you can no longer import your char from a previous game. You can import a lvl 60 char, but it only gives you some small perks for your new level 1 char...
- The skill system has been "dumbed down" or refined as I would say. Van Helsing traditionally offered lots of skills that were locked behind a progress wall and realistically not feasible to invest in, unless you want to respec and completely rebuild your character perhaps. This time around there are less skills, but they look more meaningful. Since I don't hardcore this game I don't really care that much. It's a short and cheap trip.
- The setting is as hauntingly beautiful as ever with improved graphics and effects. Nothing to dislike here if you liked the first 2 games. Also in comparison to VH2 this one does seem to offer a bit more diverse landscapes up to now (about 50% completed).
- The music is also again very great.
- Voice acting still ok.
- Story is more confusing and kind of loses sight of the supposed main villain...again, which is said. Side quests are still fun.
- The Lair is back and as annoying as it was before.
- The humour is also still there.
- The difficulty seems to be a bit better balanced. Although you can still die in 1 hit on casual...lol
- Some features have been removed: For example you can no longer switch weapon and skill sets, which is a bit sad. I also haven't found any scrolls yet and runeforging seems to be gone as well. Also health and mana potions have been removed and replaced by a cd "skill", which is basically exactly the same system minus you don't have to collect or shop for them anymore all the time, which is a great addition really, because money was never really the problem anyway. What IS weird though is that in the game you still have short cuts and even empty buttons for removed features. That's lazy...and misleading.
Basically, if you liked VH 1+2 for the story and setting you will also like this one. If you liked them because of their character and skill system you may be disappointed by this title.
What people need to realize is that all 3 VH games only cost 35 euros at most (without any DLC, probably around 50 with), which is still cheaper than most "higher quality" ARPGs out there. For that you get 3 different "episodes", the last one being quite different in terms of class design, of the same game, which gives you about 30 hours I'd say for 1 playthrough, which is adequate.
All in all it's not a bad game and so far I have not encountered any bugs or crashes, so there is no reason for me not to recommend the game for a quick joy ride. Apparently the level cap is now 30, but then again, you have more characters to try your hand with and let's see what DLC they release. There is supposedly and endless mode and scenarios as well as multiplayer, so have at it.

I have never in my whole life sworn at a game as much as I have at this game.   The controls infuriate me beyond belief.      I've read some of the other negative comments, but I have played isometric puzzlers since Ant Attack on the ZX81 and Marble Madness on the AtariST.  It's not the NW/NE/SW/SE thing that really irritates me (as it does others), it's the way the controls REACT DIFFERENTLY BASED ON THE AMOUNT OF STUFF ON THE SCREEN!!!
You're a cube, and unlike most cube games where you ROLL along nicely, in this game, there's inertia and proper physics.  Have you ever tried to ROLL a cube?  It's about as much fun as shaving your privates.  It's why the square wheel never really took off.
The Physics engine is tied to the frame rate, so when there's less on the screen, the cube reacts a lot faster to your controls, and falls back at a different rate too.  So a light tap on the up key in one part of a level might allow you to lift yourself gently and get some 'edge time', while at another, it'll flip you boldy completely over two tiles and into the chasm.
The name, and the point of the game are to 'hang' on your 'edges', but hanging on edges is  so flipping HARD with keys.  I've worn a little gap in the surface of my down arrow repeatedly trying to get the 60 second edge-time achievement (bloody hard).
So, What do I think about the game?  It's music and aesthetics are okay..  The controls are clunky, variable, and highly annoying.    The level design is interesting and sometimes actually fun.
Would I recommend this game?  If you haven't played Rush yet, yes.  If you've already played Rush, then this will be more of the same, with a much more irritating control system.   The only thing which really makes this stand out are the mobile levels which 'morph' on the click of a button.  That was fun.. But the 'click a button, then dodge a piece of flying platform' mechanic gets old.
Yes, if this game is a few quid, get it, play it, then move on.  I'd give it a 'Meh' out of 10.
ADVICE: Play this game on a high-end PC and frame limit it to 60fps.  Then the controls will at least be uniform across the game.

Torchlight 2: Action Roleplaying Isometric Lootfest featuring a solid vanilla game that can be finely tuned to preference thanks to a wide variety of Workshop content.
For fans of: Diablo, Path of Exile, Grim Dawn, basically any Isometric ARPG Lootfest that you can think of.
Four different classes:
Berserker: Fast, primarily dual-wielding melee DPS class that can summon spirits
Engineer: Heavy Armor-preferred class, utilizing two-handers or a shield and weapon with various DPS, Tank, and Support abilites. Utilizes Charge built up in combat to enhance certain abilities' effects.
Outlander: Ranged-based dps with various skills revolving around and enhancing bows, guns, and crossbows.
Embermage: Spell-based glass cannon with various elemental-based spells
Featuring:
-Four acts, each taking on a new theme and a slew of new foes, elite mobs, and bosses to fight
-Rich and beautifully designed world and characters, bringing its own art style to the table
-Charge bars, allowing classes to gain unique and powerful buffs when filled through consistent fighting in combat
-Optional Randomizable Overworld
-Randomized dungeon layouts
-Four difficulties and a Hardcore Mode if you like the thrill of Perma-Death like myself
-Up to New Game +5, with the potential to skip up to NG +3 depending on level
-Online play that is Mod-Compatible with up to four players and ten mods
-Up to 100 levels to achieve
-Randomized End-Game Dungeons for those that have conquered the Main Story
This game is a must-have for any Isometric ARPG fans and a steal at the price it's at. It's a good time by yourself, a blast with friends, and incredible amounts of replayability between both the vanilla content and the additional content you can find in the Steam Workshop. Each class plays completely different from the other with a ton of ways you can build your skills, stat points, and gear, giving you a variety of flavors for your gameplay. Any time you feel the need to spice it up, there's a mod for it. If there's something you don't like about the base game, chance's are there's a mod for it.
Don't sit on this one if you've been on the fence about it, this title is worthy of sitting in any ARPG fan's library.

is a traditional loot driven ARPG. However, some part of me feels like it'll always be seen as the younger brother so to speak in reference to the Diablo series or even the more aesthetically
Grim Dawn. Being much more fanciful, cartoonish and boisterous in it's color palette. It seemingly takes on the persona of something less daunting.
I've heard many scoff at ARPG's citing things as though they should not have an 'endgame' as if the player should not expect the character they've spent the last 30+ hours with to no longer progress after what within the genre are traditionally very lite narratives. Stating that proper MMO's need only this often proverbial

For a genre that is inherently a sort of active real-time loot driven clicker, to deny the similarities between it and how a traditional instance based MMO behaves is a bit of an asinine claim. They are inherently just slightly more repetitive than your average game. All games are repetitive. ARPG's offer repeated clicking, number crunching, finding synergies between abilities, armor and weapons. The very essence of this genre is a glorified clicker. Of ♥♥♥♥ing course it should have an endgame. I realize Path of Exile is more integrated online but aside from the towns being populated by non-NPC players the actual minute to minute is remarkably similar.
But that is neither here nor there, I bring this up only to illustrate that after a hard fought campaign with your chosen class; there are a plethora of options available to continue leveling your character. Not only is there NG+ and NG++ but there is also the Mapworks. Which essentially is a place where you can use in-game gold to purchase randomly generated maps often with qualifiers like monsters have increased damage or 25% of your max health is capped. The campaign is about 30 hours give or take and will land your character in the 50's as far as level. With each level increasing in XP reaching a maximum total of 100. There is additionally difficulty levels placed on top of these increasing difficult challenges.
There are also a ton of mods in the steam workshop. Overhaul mods, class mods, UI mods, custom dungeon mods for use in the mapworks. I personally have an Engineer, EmberMage and a modded class of Dread Pirate I'm currently leveling.

One of the best games representing Early Access, honestly. It's definitely still being actively developed, but the core structure is all there and it's all great. The momentum system is very reminiscent of the 2D Sonic games, but the emphasis here is less on precision platforming and more on maintaining that momentum through the fast-paced levels.
You have a jump button and a slide button that makes you gain speed on slopes or other downward surfaces. It seems simple, but it gives way for a lot of little complexities; you can jump onto slopes to sacrifice speed early on but gain more in the long run, jump-boost off of slopes to gain a brief burst of speed in exchange for your momentum, etc. Though pro players have already optimized most of the easier levels, there's still room for creativity to get the best possible times.
There's a few level-specific mechanics, like a grappling hook that functions similarly to the one in SpeedRunners. But for the most part, it's very focused on mastering the main mechanics, which I think is a good way to go. The game feel is sharpened to a razor sheen and it shows. The inclusion of ghosts to race against and an instant level reset button are fantastic features to foster a speedrunning community.
The style might be a little divisive, but I think it's pretty rad. 80s/90s-era action figures racing on tracks made from your usual construction materials; wood blocks, Hot Wheels tracks, that sort of thing. The action figures themselves are, for lack of a better term, butt-ugly. Which is clearly what they're going for here, so I commend them on the unique choice of character style.
Action Henk is pretty clearly tailored toward the speedrunning community, since you'll burn through most of the levels in an afternoon if you're not looking to get all the medals or compete for the best times. But I still think you'll have a good time with it either way, if you love platformers with a big focus on speed like I do.

Let me start off by saying I haven't finished the game in its entirety yet... so I may end up changing my review down the line.
I originally bought Arkham Asylum because:
A. Batman is awesome
B. It was on sale &
C. The reviews were great!
So far though I've been pretty disappointed with the quality of the game overall. I decided to write this review because this is one of the first games I've bought that was so highly reviewed which I did not thoroughly enjoy. To sum the plot of the game in a sentence you're running around as batman beating up on and catching the classic batman villians who have escaped their cells with the help of the joker. The whole story thus far seems to dragging for me it doesn't seem interesting in the slightest. The characters seem more annoying than anything and batman lacks any personality at all (although that's generally how his character is supposed to be). Whenever you die, which tends to happen frequently to me at times, the main villian you're fighting at the time will appear on the screen and taunt you for about 10 seconds or so; though interesting and fun at first it quickly became very annoying with frequent deaths/boss battles/screw ups while trying to save people. Generally when you die in a game you want to be able to pick back up again right away, at the very least the developers could have made this scene skippable. The only other problem I have with the characters, which is minor, is that the graphic art on the character details screen looks pretty amateur... One other thing that really turned me off to this game is how difficult simple things tend to be... there have been multiple instances when you're supposed to save civilians and you end up having to redo things like twenty times in order to save them because the game tends to not explain things very well. It also doesn't show where you need to go or do very well either, when pressing tab it will give you a list telling you things you need to do but at certain times it won't give you a specific location to go making you feel lost.
Overall the game still feels somewhat enjoyable despite my complaints but I wouldn't buy it for any less than 75% off.

The game is build around randomly generated levels where you need to find a key before you can fight the boss. After defeating the boss you progress to the next level. There are 5 levels total on Normal. Experience is gained by XP gems that monsters drop so you want to clear all rooms to level up the most. Also secret, treasure and danger rooms grant special items. Most weapons have a nice feel to them and are fun to shoot. The gameplay actually seems like a mix of Serious Sam (shooting, enemies) and Binding of Isaac (permadeath, new unlocks after every run, maps). Unlocks are lore, bestiary, items (perks, amulets, weapons) and characters you can play. Lore is found randomly on maps while bestiary, items and characters unlock as you play. But it would be nice to have a menu that shows you what skills and perks each character has instead of having to go into the game to find out. Very important is health management as that is only regenerated through health vials dropped by enemies or by perks. You do not carry over items, each run starts from scratch. After each death/victory you get rewards based on how many levels you finished. Overall a really fun shooter game that makes each run count and you'll spend a LOT of hours in it trying out all the various items it has to offer.
Noteworthy early perk is Wrecking Ball which can go up to level 5, you gain life by destroying objects and it helps a TON. Later you will get better perks and new characters who come with their special perks.

The PC isn’t much better; I had hoped to play him more like myself but sadly you can select the action and never the tone. Always Sometimes Monsters is a creative RPG that was created by Vagabond Dog and published by Devolver Digital. It is available on Steam for the low price of $10. In Always Sometimes Monsters, you have just lost the love of your life and you have not payed the rent of the month to the landlord. The landlord takes your keys, leaving you homeless when you receieve an invitation that the love of your life is marrying another man. You decide to go and interfere, causing a series of events to occur as you try to get to the wedding by the end of the month.
Story - For the ten minutes I was very confused. Then, the story began to unfold letting me know I had to get to this girl in x amount of days or else it's all over. I have actually never seen this type of story in a game, so I definitely found it quite interesting to go through. There were surprises at every turn that allowed the game to go into more depth and the story is definitely worth an honorable mention.
Graphics  - As mentioned above, this is an RPG game, a 2D one at that. This game was created on the RPG Maker, but it excels in what the engine gives it with some very smooth looking character models and creative art for the buildings. Saying that, the graphical art is definitely not spectacular, but it definitely fits with the RPG style of the whole game, which is more than many developers can say.
Controls - The controls do take some getting used to, but they are definitely not "clunky". The controls definitely could have been better, but they work and they work with little to no response time.
Fun Factor - I was very eager to play on the game, actually staying up later in the night than any other game that has released this year, which definitely means something. The replayablity of this game is very high as you can pick different decisions and some have a big difference in the game, which is one of the things I enjoy the most about this game.
Recap Negatives - The controls could have been better, but were overall good. The graphics are nothing special, yet it is an RPG, so take that into consideration.
Final Score:  9/10

This is a poor man's spelunky. But I don't mean it in a bad way.
A long time ago, when my internet connection was bad, and while waiting for a game to download I needed to wait around 4 hours for it to complete downloading, I kept looking for something to do while the game is downloading in the background.
I came across Kongregate, a site that features flash games which are sent by it's users.
*Fade in Epic Music*
I was astounded to see how much flash games evolved. From "Bloon Tower Defense 2" we've evolved to "Gem Craft", from "Yeti Olympics" to that game with a giant Minotaur wrestling through candyland.  Flash Games had achievements, Unlockables, Multiple features that were up 'till now used by AAA titles, 2D Call of Duty clones with Borderlands-like loot (Strike Force Heroes 2, it's kinda grindy, but it's fun if you've got the time) that felt fun to play, even solo!
In that specific site I came across developers Nerdook, who's games kept popping at the site. While his game featured minimalistic, nearly unappealing graphics, they almost always had that addictive element that got you playing and kept you glued to the game a few more minutes.
Now, I HATE roguelike-esque games. they don't appeal to me, they feel too repetitive and I get bored with them very easily, However, this one, however, for some unknown reason, I'm having a blast with. Maybe it's the fact it's so easy to pick up, casual, yet, Well built enough to seem more advanced than it's actually is. Simple, yet Complex enough to feature a lot of content.
I'll try to summarize the game in points:
Pros
+Easy to pick up.
+You can play small session or try to run through it, time is no issue in this game.
+Split Screen!
+Tons of characters and stuff to unlock.
+It's simple, casual fun.
Can't Decide
=Music is great at times, other times, not so great.
=Randomly Generated Platforming. It's good, but sometimes has it's issues.
Cons
-Design feels a bit flawed to me. Unappealing.
-It might be irritating for people who are looking for more of a challenge, I got to level 5 and feel like it's not going to be too hard to complete the game.. however it might change later, will edit accordingly.
-Price. I mean, I got this game for free, so I have no complaints, but just to compare, Plants vs. Zombies GOTY is 5$ and has more content, maybe I'm just being a cheapskate, but that's me.
Overall I recommend this game to everyone who like short runs through randomly generated dungeons for treasure, also if you wanted spelunky but it was too expensive for you.

The Incredible Adventures of Van Helsing III is about Van Helsing's son, Abraham, and his ghostly companion. The third installment focused more on Katarina's backstory. We learned her origin story in this game and how she became a ghost. The story telling is about what you would expect if you've ever played a Van Helsing game then you'll be right at home with the witty dialogue and action combat.
The Good:
Gameplay:
If you've ever played an ARPG you'll know what to expect here. Tons of monsters, loot, and quest for you to do while you level up your character until you reach the level cap so you can farm for legendary gear or make a new class. It's no different here, but The Incredible Adventures of Van Helsing is different than your typical Diablo game. Van Helsing games have always had a mix of tower defense segments in them. Deathtrap is a good example of how they'll play out and if you don't know what Deathtrap is I encourage you to read my review here.
The major difference that sets The Incredible Adventures of Van Helsing III apart from it's predecessors are the six new character classes. I originally thought that these new classes would be available alongside the three we already had, but I was mistaken. The original three character classes from Van Helsing I and II are gone, but I'll go more into detail later on this review.
You'll obviously run into a lot of loot while you're out slaying monsters and you'll probably be making frequent trips back to your secret hideout or you can just give Lady Katarina all of your loot and let her sell it for you. This is a really great mechanic and I'm glad it's still present in the game.
Soundtrack:
The soundtrack here easily beats both Van Helsing I and II. The opening menu theme is beautiful and it really sets the tone of the game. Every track fits the stage it's on nicely and it really added to the experience for me. The only track I didn't like was the final boss one. It was just your average encounter music.
Six Character Classes:
As I stated above there are six character classes in The Incredible Adventures of Van Helsing III. All of them are vastly different than each other. I enjoyed my playthrough as an elementalist, but I do wish the skill tree was a lot deeper. In Van Helsing II we had over 20 magical skills to master over the course of our playthrough. In Van Helsing III we only have 8 and I beat the game only using two of them.
Story:
I was originally going to place this in the bad section of this review, but learning what happened to Lady Katarina and saving the world helped to place it in the positive section. There is nothing groundbreaking about the story here, but it gets the job done. I was disappointed in more than a few parts of the story, but I enjoyed the ending to the game. I would say it's a toss up between good and bad, but I enjoyed it more than I hated it.
In Van Helsing III your former ally, Prisoner 7, has betrayed you and is trying to convert the world back into the way it was in the past and to do that he's using the Ink to shape everything in his image. Van Helsing must save the day once again and get his revenge at the same time.
The Bad:
You Can't Import Your Old Characters:
This is probably my biggest problem with the game right now. All of that hard work I did going through both Van Helsing I and II was pointless. Why let us get attached to our old characters if you were never going to let us finish the trilogy with him?
The New Skill Tree Looks Nice, But It's Lacking:
There's no denying that the new skill tree in Van Helsing III looks better than it ever did, but we only have a fraction of the skills that we had in previous games. The only two spells that I used throughout my entire playthrough was my two lightning spells. The ice spells are useless and the only cool fire spell is the summon that you get, but what's the point of that when I one hit just about everything with my lightning?
The passive skill tree is still there, but it's also been gutted to hell and back. I don't understand why they decided to dumb the game down so much. Is it because it's going to the Xbox One?
Level 30 Cap:
The Incredible Adventures of Van Helsing II had a level 60 level cap. The Incredible Adventures of Van Helsing III took it down to 30 for some reason. Why? Your guess is as good as mine. That's not the only thing that went down though. The game is way too easy. I started playing this morning and beat it a few hours later. It took me hours upon hours of gameplay to reach the level cap in Van Helsing I. It took me 7 hours to reach it in part III...
You Can't Buy Healing Potions Anymore:
Who thought it would be a good idea to take away our healing potions? I really want to know this so I can slap them in the face. Why would you take potions out of an ARPG? Instead of potions we get a single health/mana potion that takes an eternity to cooldown for another usage. Give me back my potions. I liked having over 100 of them.
No Neverending Story:
Every Van Helsing game had a Neverending Story mode. It's Van Helsing's version of a new game plus. It ramps up the difficulty and lets up play through the game as many times as we want. Why is it missing in here? The only thing I got after I completed the game was Scenario Mode, but I never really liked that mode.
Little To None Replayability:
Since there's no Neverending Story I don't really feel like jumping back in this game and I just started it today. I feel like Neocore Games ran out of funding for this game and just released it as is.
Van Helsing III Is Nearly Unplayable Right Now:
The Incredible Adventures of Van Helsing III is filled with bugs. I had to figure out a way, by myself by the way, to enter the game. The developers had no idea what was causing my game crash. I can't even play this online right now because the game will only turn on in offline mode. I've walked on floors that were missing textures, and fell through the floor to my death a few times. There is a ton of missing dialogue. I could be talking to an npc that I'm actually interested in and the dialogue would just skip itself and go to the next line. This game was not ready to be released. It feels like a beta some times.
The Verdict:
The Incredible Adventures of Van Helsing III right now is the weakest game in the trilogy. I have no idea what the devs were thinking when they stripped this game down and released it. I love the gameplay and I love Van Helsing, but I think I'll stick to parts 1 and 2 before I touch part 3 again. I'll wait until there's more content and I'll consider writing about this again one day, but I'm really disappointed that series ended this way.

I really enjoyed this game, it's a solid ARPG and a lot of fun, but why don't I recommend it? As a big fan of the series since the first game, I can't help but be majorly disappointed.
The jump from Van Helsing 1 to Van Helsing 2 was pretty big. You got another large and interesting story, the level cap was doubled and the skill tree was also double. But it seems like they've taken all that back out for this installment.
The story is painfully short and feels rushed, the final boss fight is a joke and an absolute pushover, the level cap has been halved back down to 30, and the skill tree has also been dramatically reduced to a tree that's even small than the one in the original game. They try to make up for the small skill trees and low level cap by having 6 character classes instead of 3 but that opens up another problem.
The 3 original classes are gone meaning, as most other fans of the series have pointed out, no character import.
As far as I can tell, the original 3 are still there in spirit. The Hunter now being the Bounty Hunter, Arcane Mechanic now being the Constructor, and the Thaumaturge now being the Elementalist. But these classes have been changed and reduced down so much that they're just shells of their former selves.
Another thing that got to me a bit is the lack of New Game+. This is more of a personal thing to me but when I finish the game, I like to go back to the start with my high level character, and play through again on a higher difficulty like you can do in Titan Quest and Dark Souls for example.
But, does this game do anything right?
Actually yes. The gameplay itself is very enjoyable. It's a solid ARPG, it's challenging in places and there's plenty of little side areas to explore and secrets to find. The graphics are pretty and the Elementalist's skills are especially flashy! (I like pretty lights!)
Conclusion:
A fun game, but feels more of an addon to Van Helsing 2 with it's short story, reduced level cap and reduced skill trees. It does have some plus sides but as of now (26/05/2015) I can't recommend it.
I have heard that the devs will continue to add free content updates in the future, so I may come back to this review then and my opinion may change.

Great interactive story about normal real life struggles. I do not think this will resonate as much or feel as close to home for young or single folks, but for working parents the compromises and the choices the game present regarding competing priorities will feel very personal. I was 100% confident with my choices and ended up perfectly satisfied with the outcomes. I really felt like the game told "my" story in that sense.

As for the beginning i should mention that i'm a highly emotive person but cold-hearted at the same time, who could watch any emotionally disturbing events and never blink an eye if circumstances demand so, however this game didn't even bother to try me. I'll probably get assaulted by some who presumably were tackled by the emotiveness of this game, but i'll take my chances since, frankly, there is no single reason why i would give it a thumbs up.
It is indeed a game which tends to appeal on emotions, but it fails this part too, except a few occasion when it manages to touch the player, and further on i'll explain why. First of all, it's almost one year after release and the game is still buggy. You can see that for yourself in the 2 screenshots i've posted on the game's community hub. Characters can sit on invisible chairs, type on invisible typing machines or read books while their heads are stuck in the table, etc, and all of that in less than 4 hours of gaming... Also, Dan, the main character developed a habit to close the doors of his office when he needs to rest or focus on the book he's writing, and doesn't want to be disturbed by his family. I got stuck in his office for quite a few times, having nothing to do, just waiting and wondering when will he finally open the doors so i can get out. At first i relied on the fact that me being a ghost, i'm not supposed to be seen opening doors, but imagine my surprise when i saw for the first time his wife walking in the office right through the closed door, and walking out through the other one. I was like "WTF? I am the damn ghost in this house or this this family who clearly posseses more supernatural skills than i do ?!"
Leaving all bugs and glitches behind, the whole purpose of the game is to find out what the family members wish for, and try to make them all happy, or at least feeling less miserable, by choosing somebody's wish and make a compromise with other member. Problem is the choices are sometimes ridiculous. For example: the mother wants to go camping on some place far from home, the father wants to go camping somewhere near by, and the son wants his father to help him launch his toy rocket. You choose father's wish to go camping somewhere near by and try to reach a compromise with his wife based on the fact that he's behind the schedule with his work on the book. Done. The son remains unhappy. WHY ?! Even if the father is so ridiculously busy at home, why can't he just take 5 minutes and help his son launch a toy rocket while they were camping for almost an entire day? And this is only one example from an entire list of unrealistic stupid choices one has to make.
What else made me be so cold-hearted towards this game's attempt to appeal on my emotions ? The almost empty house, the dull environment, the repetitive actions of the characters which walk from a part of the house to another over and over, and mostly the lack of any active emotions between them. Upon the interaction of the characters in the house you'll just hear "Hi mom" and the answer back "Hi darling", and that's all, after which they all go do something different, mother watches TV, the son plays with a toy, and the father drinks by himself in the office or sticks his head again in the table and starts to read. Does that look like a busy family to you where they presumably can't find the time to satisfy each other ?
There are many other things i could list, but looks like my review is becoming too long, so i'll just stop here. The overall experience felt boring and tedious. There is no way i could recommend to anybody this clearly overpriced and overrated game.

9/10 - One of the best novel/epistolary driven game experiences since Dear Esther. If you are looking for action - it's not for you.
I've completed the game just now, and I would say that I am freaking amazed how a simple idea can make such a wonderful, soul-soothing, but at times - heartbreaking experience. It is a wonderful story about a family, the story that is shaped by YOU. You are a ghost, indeed, but it is not really about that. The game is called "The Novelist" because, despite the fact that Dan - the father in this family - is trying to write a book, you are actually the one who is writing a novel. You are writing a novel about the life of this family, and you make actions that are shaping the story, and I am sure this game has multiple endings, depending on what choices you make.
Dan is trying to write a novel, his wife Linda is trying her luck at painting pictures. Their kid Tommy is trying to adapt to the new environment in new school and tries to deal with dyslexia. You choose who gets the momentum, and who will be dissapointed with their days. Sometimes you will try to make VERY TOUGH descisions.... Thats how the gameplay works, and your actions will lead to different branches of the story...
I cried in the end, most of the actions I did were trying to help everyone... But that is not always how it is in real life. I cried in the end because I am going through the exact moment of my life right now. It's either my career, or my family. And in this game - i chose family. And now I am quite sure that this is what I am going to do in my life.
I salute you Orthogonal Games for writing and developing such a good, mesmerising story that could actually make me think about my choices, and maybe think about life and family in general.

The game "was" short, but it was very fulfilling, especially having done it on Stealth-mode. Being short, I feel I can even play it a few more times to see what the results will be like if I make different choices.
Some of the choices were easy to make, some were minor, but there were a few VERY tough choices. I beat the game in a few hours, but the choices, story, and affect from the characters made this feel like it went on for days, but in a VERY good way. I'm hoping for a sequel, given that there is room for it, but I don't even feel like there's much need for any change outside of making a new story and maybe a new environment.
If I had any negative comments about the game, it would be reading up on the former entries of those in the house. They were great stories too, but I felt like they didn't explain much beyond that the ghost helped people who lived there. I was hoping to find out who the ghost is or learn more about one person at a time. It seemed the stories of the past got rushed by a bit.
All-in-all, I highly recommend this game. Very easy-paced, simple, and enjoyable. A nice break from more intense games or a tense day.

-Overall Review-
Who's Your Daddy is an interactive game about a father attempting to prevent his baby from certain death. Although the description of the game seems bland, Who's Your Daddy is a very fun and addictive game with depth added into its every design. This game is one of the few games that have lots of potential, and Who's Your Daddy takes advantage of that from doing everything possible to show its true form, a well-rounded, polished, fun game. From the many different items that are used both for the baby and daddy and the realistic house, it all adds into the feeling of saving your baby or dying a horrible death. I personally enjoyed tricking my daddy by closing doors to make it look like I wasn't in the room and then grabbing a hammer, rushed to the glass table in the TV room and smashed the glass and roll in it, gloating in my glory. You can be stuck for hours in this game without realizing how much time has passed because of the little details and Easter eggs that are hidden in the game. Figuring out how to eat batteries and Clorox Bleach is just scraping the surface. From vents in the house to finding car keys to hiding in a cabinet, Who's Your Daddy distances itself from other games because of the detail to every single thing possible to see and still maintaining the fair price and continuous weekly updates that make the game better. However, all games aren't perfect. Glitches forcing you to restart the game and minor setbacks here and there are always looming above you, however Who's Your Daddy somehow distracts the player from these imperfections by giving engulfing you in every game of 1 versus 1, making you want to play more, thus creating the best experience possible. If you aren't sure about getting this game, get it now! You won't regret it.
--Pros--
Easter eggs and small details continue to pull you into the game.
Whether you are the baby or daddy, the suspense of saving the baby or hiding from the daddy is always around the corner.
Early Access continues to bring new and improved features into an already great game.
--Cons--
Often times you find yourself waiting for minutes at a time for someone to join or someone to join you.
The "servers" are not fully functional and may glitch at times.
Frustration is always there when the biggest glitch of all occurs: You and someone else start a game, and the timer does not start, forcing you to exit and restart the game.
---Verdict---
Overall despite some minor setbacks and glitches, Who's Your Daddy provides players with a plethora of items to toy around with, and the exciting baby versus daddy episodes are sure to last.

Overall I enjoyed this game. The story gave a lot of choice and presented some interesting dilemmas, although some parts did tend to drag on a little bit. I enjoyed the ending, and while I would be a little interested to see how the story can play out with different choices, the game doesn't have a lot of replay value.
Not much to say about the graphics - the screenshots basically tell you all you need to know. The art is not amazing, but decent. The music on the other hand was generally great, although some tracks were a bit irritating. The developers crammed in a bunch of references to other indie titles with collectable items, and references game that try to remind you repeatedly that you're playing an indie game right now and I found it a little annoying. There's a fair number of mini games scattered throughout the game as well, though most of them are mediocre, if not downright terrible. Thankfully, the bad ones are completely optional. The core of the game is in the narritive and managing your money. My only complaint there would be that the whole stamina system is not well explained, I was never sure what the consequences of not eating would be and was never told.
Overall, Always Sometimes Monsters is a decent game, though there are better games out there. The fact that there is so much choice tends to mean that a lot of the dialogue feels very generic and weakens the narritive. Even still, the price is right, and if you have the time to play it I'd reccomend picking it up. There are certainly better stories out there, but seeing how your version of this one plays out is worth the time.

Ziggurat is what you would get if you took 2004's "Painkiller" and gave it a roguelike makeover, with randomly generated tile-based levels and light RPG elements, but left the actual graphics and gameplay back in the previous decade.
Each new playthrough is theoretically totally different from the last, but in practice it's kinda like eating pizza for every meal, except each time you have to come up with a unique way of getting it into your mouth. The maps are all randomized, but each room template is used repeatedly, just with different challenges pasted in. The bosses are basically always the same on each of the 5 stages, and you'll run into the same assortments of mobs over and over.
The unlocks achieved through repeated playthroughs are simply variations on the existing game modes, such as new weapons or character quirks that jumble the numbers around a bit; some characters are faster, some are stronger, some regenerate, and so forth. Every time you die, you start a new game unequipped and level 1, but the new items get shuffled into the deck for random treasure assignments. Again, variety, but you're only changing the toppings on the pizza. The only real difference is whether you eat it with salad tongs, your elbows, or standing on your head.
I managed to beat it twice, after an embarassing number of tries, and even with new unlocks (and the promise of more) there's not really enough variety in the concept that I'd willingly suffer through it again. You run, you shoot, you dodge, and try not to die. Repeat until bored.
I'm sure there are some people who will never get enough of this concept, but for me, the difficulty and repetition prevent much replay value.

Batman: Arkham Asylum. This game is hands down the best superhero game of all time (in my opinioon of course). This game took the old, superhero combat system and completely reinvented it with Rocksteady's new Free-Flow combat system. Combat with enemies was no longer choppy and repetitive, but instead smooth and downright fun, as the game challened you to string together strikes, combo moves, and gadgets to take down your targets effectively. This game successfully implements both stealth and combat encounters, but more evenly, so as not to make you bored of one style. From a story standpoint, the game is fantastic. I won't give any spoilers, but I will say that not many games are actually able to bring together a group of super villains in a way that actually makes sense. The boss fights are great as well, challenging you to use all of your different gadgets in different ways to defeat each of your opponents. Another thing that hardcore Batman fans will enjoy are the references. In Arkham Asylum, the implementation of Riddler trophies, riddles, and the Arkham recordings provide a plethera of Batman universe goodness. There are tons of these little "easter eggs" that contain pieces of information on tons of DC characters. Overall, I would say that Batman: Arkham Asylum is not only the best game in the Arkham Series, and a legendary game in of itself, but a huge success for Rockteady. I would rate this game a 10/10.

Full review:
Vertical Drop Heroes is a Rogue LITE platformer game with procedually generated level similar to rogue legacy.
Start off a run-get killed-upgrade
Along the way,you will see merchants randomly spawn around the map.Each merchant will offer whether a trait or a ability.
Traits and spells-It is randomly given to "class" or "heroes" to help you along in your run
In your run you will encounter some NPC that will give you quest that you can choose to complete the game's currency
In every level you will encounter a Big enemy-also called as a boss-that you must either defeat it or use 5keys to proceed to the next level
You will also encounter caged up "heroes" that can be freed using keys,heroes will help you until they die or when you carry on to the next level
Maps are randomly generated with different mechanics(filled with bombs etc,etc)
"totems" or "statues" are randomly spread around the level that can help you by activating them using the game's currency
Pros
-Graphic fits into the theme of the game
-TONS OF traits and spells you can unlock that can greatly affects your gameplay
-different"class" that have different loadout
-Interesting map design
-Great potential time waster
Cons
-Rng decides where traps and enemy are placed(forced to go through traps to progress through the level)tough this does not happen often,it's frustrating when it happens
The amount of content and replayability fully justify the game price.Trust me,you're going to have alot of fun playing this game

First off: I got this game for free from some giveaway so I felt sorta bad giving it a negative review, but in the end I decided that a frustrating gift is strill frustrating and someone might be buying this game with his money so here I am.
Someone called this game "Rogue Legacy Lite" and personally I think he was high on meth or pcp. Real talk though I see where the comparision is coming from: it's a 'roguelike' game where you get a new character with somewhat random statistics and perks influenced by what you uncover via playing the game. I can see the developers being strongly influenced by Rogue Legacy but they took a wrong path midway.
I want to start with the menu and first impression. Game's got 3 gamemodes: single player, splitscreen and LAN. Alright, why is there LAN, but no Online option? You can fool no one, this doesn't require much more work, nobody asks you to run a server, let one of the players be the server, come on. Another thing: why is there no volume control? Why is autoattack set to ON on default? I'm gonna talk about that in a second, cause that's SOMETHING completely different.
You start the game, ready to rock, you spawn in some sort of a chamber (which is kinda nice) and they introduce you to very basics of upgrading stuff and there's even some nice "teasers" of what's about to come. Then you start the actual level and oh boy, is it fun.
Well, first thing's first: the audio is just... crackling? The levels are too high sometimes and it seems like it never got compressed which leads to you hearing crackling noises, but it's only a minor annoyance. Overall the music and sound effects are just average. Nothing special, nothing memorable, but not really annoying or bad.
The gameplay's whole lotta worse. When you first play this game it's ok and sorta fun, then you start realizing it's EXTREMELY repetitive, every level has got the same basic pattern and some mechanics are really frustrating. Most weapons are basically melee and you're bound to get hit by most enemies, except for the ones who stand still and have long attack cooldown. For all the other kinds of enemies you just get hit when you hit them, unless you're being extremely careful and the enemy stands in place due to the fact he's got nowhere to run.
Game offers "Pacifist runs" (without killing the enemies) and for the most part, at beginning I was wondering how that works. It doesn't really pay off for the most part, unless you're willing to backtrack and kill all the enemies after completing a pacifist run. Also the first couple of times I tried it I couldn't do it because I would end up killing people unwillingly 90% of the time. Mostly due to the random nature of the game. Sometimes enemies can be placed in a way that you HAVE TO take a hit and since AUTOATTACK IS ON AT DEFAULT you end up killing them as well. So, disable the autoattack and you can complete a sado-masochistic run, you don't even benefit from (only in some special cases).
Even though the platforms and 'blocks' are placed randomly, it's always in the weirdest patterns with horrible enemy placement, none of the runs are memorable and due to how every level is made (just a vertical level with a boss on the very bottom), it gets boring REALLY fast. I tried to play that game for as long as I could without killing myself or driving myself to psychosis, and I didn't perservere for long.
It's not that this game is completely bad, but they tried to 'remix' a concept and failed. It doesn't feel good. Mechanics are weird. Balancing is done poorly (why are damage upgrades done in step of +1, why not make a more expensive upgrade of +3 and then balance it better?). I think developers also KNEW the fighting system and enemy placement was terrible and you were about to get hit by EVERYTHING, and that's why they decided you're gonna level up every 5 enemies and replenish your HP that way. Jumping controls are a bit off. Why is there limited ammo for ranged weapons (to elaborate a bit: I know why, but this isn't the right solution, since you're basically forcing players to save it up for bosses, because they can't allow to trade hits with them)? Why are all the upgrades so 'meh' (actually 'unlocks'). Why is this entire game such a 'MEH'?
Playing this game feels like cheesing it, there's no appeal to it whatsoever, it's pretty bad, gets boring quickly and no amount of recycling ideas from Rogue Legacy or Godlike (♥♥♥♥ that game, seriously) is gonna fix it. Fix the basics, play your own game a bit, balance it and maybe it might become playable.

Batman Arkham Asylum is the first in what would end up becoming a popular franchise. Its a third person action/adventure where you're tasked with stopping one of the
Joker's nefarious new plans involving Arkham Asylum. It features a much darker story than saturday morning fare, more akin to the Christopher Nolan films and the comics.
If you're a fan of batman already this game has everything you want: gritty story and visuals, all kinds of bat-gadgets, and satisfying hand-to-hand combat. The presentation is grim and sets a fantastic backdrop for everything that takes place. The voice acting is superb featuring many classic voice actors including Mark Hamil reprising his legendary role as the Joker. Arkham Asylum is a lengthy game looking at 12+ hours at the minimum, with lots to explore and secrets to collect. Despite all the content already available dont expect to see too many famous villains crammed into one game as the developers obviously had sequels in mind, but the villians it did give us fit into the story perfectly.
>PROS
Faithful to the franchise
Dark and gritty visuals and presentation
Combat and Puzzles are fun and hardly get boring
Boss battles are varied and interesting
Fantastic Voice Acting
Great graphics with attention to detail
Harley Quinn & Poison Ivy
>CONS
Minor bugs in the V1.1 Release
Sometimes feels slightly repetitive
Ending could have been better
Bottom line: A ruby the size of a tangerine.

Alright, this game was actually for me a really gray area on whether to recommend or not. The reason I selected recommend is because the quality of the game really comes down to being your own choice on whether its good or not.
I am a highly competitive persom
--- Not in particular, however, the ranked system does do (In my opinion) a great job on placing you with people who are challenging to play against.
--- This is where my first comment about it being your choice comes in. Sometimes someone knows a lot of strings/combos and people get♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥when they constantly use the same combo/string to beat you. Same goes with items, some people run around and hide a lot while chucking shiza at you constantly avoiding any real conflict. If you can deal with this every once and awhile then you will most definately have a great time during ranked fights.
--- The community can be a party-pooper when it comes to ranked play specifically. There is no shortage of "EZ" or "Just quit the game bro!" among other clever remarks after game results. It is a great opportunity to practice your patience and gain a valuable life skill, however this is another one of those moments where however you feel about this really effects how you'll like this game
The selection of Legends is great as well as the mechanics of each. I think this game is a hard to learn hard to master situation, at first your gunna really hate how badly you can get thrashed, but eventually you appreciate it even when you take a bad beating.
So I really really recommend this for cool heads and perhaps pro-ish gamers. But if your a hot head or you really just suck at video games, I would stick with Super Smash Brothers.

A cult classic. This game has an awesome story, the smoothest controls*, a good amount of side content, and fairly low hardware requirments. Man this game. Where do I begin?
The atmosphere just gets you right in the gut from the beginning of the game. Filling you inside this disturbed and twisted asylum filled with the beloved Batman characters we all know today. It's pretty damn good for just the beginning of the game. It starts already with you capturing Joker, which is a change in pace of the typical Batman stuff we know. However it has, dare I say, realism aspects in the game. This changes the overall mood and pace; this game wants you to take it seriously and they convey a good job of that.
The controls are tight and compact. I rarely have issues with them other than some hiccups here and there, but it's rare. It feels very comfortable and smooth, where even the most basic of games like Left 4 Dead have some problems with gamepad support, dispite the limitations. I was playing with a gamepad this run, so the keyboard and mouse may have more polished controls than the standard, though I digress.
The characters have, duh, character. The basic batman shows and comics have the same idea, though this game makes it all well and good. I was wondering what character would act like what, and it just left me guessing over and over.
My favorite part was the scarecrow sequences. It was just plain brilliant. It had some scare factor, and a level of difficulty to the game. It breaks the action from the typical game and throws you for a loop each sequence: even going as far to break the 4th wall entirely.
The ending, however wasn't very polished. For the sake of people wanting to know themselves, I won't spoil this. Though I admit it could be done a little better.
Overall, give this game your money. I mean it. It deserves it. And it deserved Game of the Year. Get it. Now.

Brawlhalla is a very good game clearly inspired by Super Smash Bros. I'm not big on fighting games because of 3 things:
-Bad matchmaking
-Heavy reliance on combos for max damage
and
-Combos that are hard to pull off.
Brawlhalla suffers from all those. But first the pros and cons.
Pros
-Range of characters with different weapons and attacks
-Sick combos you can use on your enemies
-Ranking up is easy
-You can bloody spank your enemies while they continuously bounce off walls
-Lots of customisation
-A bind that makes you say gg
Cons
-Matchmaking is bad. It will always match you with more experienced players than players your skill level.
-Heavy reliance on combos. Meaning you will barely do any damage with normal attacks
-Most combos are hard to pull off. Combos happen by pressing w,a,s,d while left and right clicking. Simple right? Well not really. Sometimes you will do the incorrect move and stuff up your combos when you even did the right combination.
-Players K.O you in the cheapest ways. Such as standing on a edge waiting to smash you again until you die.
-On top of all that combo rant. Combos can be easily dodged and interrupted by others.
-Levels are way too similar
-Spam. Too much spam. The mostly flat stages you fight on also increases the amount of spam as there is nowhere to go.
-Gravity Cancels are clutches to pull off ground attacks in the air. Seriously, if you want to do ground combos, get your opponent on the floor like a real man.
Overall, Brawlhalla is an awesome fighting game that has its traits and its flaws. Early access means this can be changed. However at the moment. This is a game I'll play for a while, then leave it and maybe return because of an update or a friend of mine has bought it. But I give it a thumbs up because it has massive potential. At the moment, I main Mordex.

Within the first few hours, you're already questioning all the good guys, regretting some decisions you made, having 10 minute long political debates with heavily armed metal lugs, and catching multiple refrerences to Dr. Strangelove - oh, and spilling a few Russian people's drinks (look up "I Spill My Drink!") This game couldn't be more Deus Ex, unless it was called "The Illuminati Conspiracy".
Everytime I take the "naturals' section I get stopped at customs. Just like Witcher, you play an outsider, but this time instead of a hero, you're just a super-powered lowlife in the eyes of the populous. It's such a great dichotomy of power and hopelessness that makes such a rich, interesting world. The class struggle is really played out here, with naturals doing everything they can to fight augmented people as a means of showing they are more human than them.
Combat and stealth are redefined, and are really great. This game can make you feel like a♥♥♥♥♥♥for taking the non-lethal action, just as it can the other way around, and that's a really special skill in such a deep world.

Really does give you the feeling that you can play the way you want (even though I was a stealth murder-hobo) It does seem to have decent replayablility just based off each of the individual missions and how you act as well (We'll just say murder-hoboing usually ends with people dead rather than alive.... who woulda thought.) Then they had to go and mess up the DLC's (which I got one as my preorder purchase but have not bought any of the others). The issue with the DLC's is that they are supposed to take place at certain parts of the story but you get to play them later (for whatever reason, probably just cutting things so they have an excuse for the season pass). Normally that wouldn't be much of an issue, but it's the fact that they are like seperate mini-games. They give you some skill points and measly weapons but in no way does it actually hold up to your character because they give you crap and get rid of everything else. If the DLC's actually took place in the main campaign where they were supposed to it wouldn't be an issue its the fact that they are completely seperate and then PUNISH you for playing them. This is the same thing they did with the last Deus Ex (They eventually had a patch that fixed that and put the mission in the main game but still). I just want them to cut the crap and fix it. I love the game and the series but I don't think I can recommend buying day one anymore. Hitman (another square enix title but developed by IO interactive) was another issue. If at least for Square Enix I'm done buying games Day One from huge publishers. Oh but I still recommend the game. It's good.

While there technically are no "wrong" or "right" decisions, I couldn't help but find myself to choose the more, erm, "sound" ones. But either way, depending on what you do, the story changes and I really enjoyed that. The extra stories of the previous tennats were a nice addition. There are hints everywhere of interesting directions the game could have taken, but it manages to avoid all of them. The ending result is a bland, dull and completely unremarkable experience.

Let me just start off by saying I got this game because at one point in my life, I had a strong passion for writing.  I still hold writing to be important to me, but it will no longer be my career of choice. As such, after hearing numerous stories of how taxing writing a book can be for the average author, be it on their sanity, nerves, love life, or even the amount of time able to be allocated to quality family fun, I really hoped to both emulate that and hear another good story in this game. That, and the fact that it seemed like it'd play out simlar to Heavy Rain, or Fahrenheit (The Indigo Prophecy).
Now, the game itself spins a good story, but not nearly enough as I'd expect from a game all about writing, and titled "The Novelist". The story is too simple, and the choices you can make lack any real sense of worth to the other characters, or even yourself, if you choose to have Dan focus on his book. The choices you must decide on in this game can be easily compounded together to satisfy all parties, with good time management (which I guess Dan does not have). Gameplay is also very repeditive, stealth mode or not, and offers no creativity. The "compromises" are very disappointing, and seem to have even more of a negative imapct on the family than just choosing one solution to one person's desires.
The game also fails to lift any emotion from me, as the voice acting sounds forced, unemotional, and half♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ to be frank. Many lines are very cheesy, melodramatic, and sound as if taken out of a cancelled soap opera. Many of the Visual Novels here on Steam have more tear-jerking moments than this entire game does, and that speaks volumes, considering the VNs on Steam are half♥♥♥♥♥♥♥themselves, short, and were made solely for a quick buck on Steam.
I digress.
This game does not meet or even come close to the potential satisfaction it could have delivered by such a unique concept in a game; therefore, I cannot reccomend it. For me, not only was it the potential wasted that made me not want to reccomend this game, it was the fact that none of the story even evoked the tiniest bit of empathy within me. It lacked heart, and emotion into the voices, and the dialogue itself.
Don't even consider spending more than $4.

Always Sometimes Monsters represents the worst kind of stupid game: it is a stupid game that calls itself a brilliant work of art.
ASM is advertised as a story-driven experience, but ASM’s narrative is at best silly and at worst downright dumb. The plot involves slowly meandering through less than a handful of sparsely populated, small towns to dissuade a former lover from marrying someone else. Along the way, decisions must be made about whether to be nice or mean to uninspired, cardboard cut-out NPCs.
You are never really provided a reason to care about the former lover. You are simply expected to care about her/him. This expectation applies to all the other flimsily developed NPCs as well. Sometimes they have problems involving drug-use, sex, violence, suicide, etc., but these subjects are never thoughtfully explored.  "Mature content" is inserted as if merely including it is enough to elicit emotional investment in the characters and story--but the trivialization of sophisticated issues only comes off as a failed attempt to be "edgy."
Clumsy, unpolished writing also plagues the entire game. Dialogue between the protagonist and NPCs is uncreative, insipid, and dull-witted. Characters often spew unnecessary profanity like children who say “bad words” to sound “cool.” And when ASM isn’t transparently trying to be provocative, it bludgeons you with trite declarations about life, choices, and consequences. The ponderous tone of these statements gives an impression of self-importance, rather than intelligence. While playing, I couldn't help imagining the folks at Vagabond Dog spouting this stuff to each other and saying "that's deep, man."
Actually, I didn't have to imagine much because ASM's creators apparently think shoving themselves into the game at every available opportunity is clever.
Pixelated versions of the creators stand atop the Delvolver logo. They make an appearance during character selection. They show up in every coffee shop of every town. They even squeeze themselves into the epilogue. And their dialogue often consists of praise of ASM's content and comments such as “whoa, meta.” Maybe the cameos would be less irritating if there were more NPCs (and more stimulating NPCs) to interact with, but the NPC population dwindles as the game progresses.
Instead of repeatedly congratulating themselves, the team at Vagabond Dog should have focused on making ASM a better game.
Definitely, not recommended.

Alot of people say this game is like Super Smash Bros, and while that is partially true, it is also very incorrect.
Brawlhalla is if the original Super Smash brothers was given a new mechanic, skins, more characters and updated graphics, while also taking out smash attacks entirely. IN MY OPINION every smash bros, except Brawl,  after Smash 64 (The original smash bros for the nintendo 64) is better than Brawlhalla. This includes: Smash bros Melee, Smash Bros for 3DS, Smash Bros for Wiiu and the very popular Project M mod for Smash Bros Brawl. Before people start to get their panties in a knot, alow me to explain. Like I said, this is like smash 64 with a new mechanic and better graphics, meaning it doesn't have smash attacks, a very important staple to the smash series. For those who haven't played a smash bros game, smash attacks serve as basic attacks that can be charged to become stronger, but are not the only basic attack, you have 4 smash attacks for each direction but also have what are known as tilts for the same directions. With Brawlhalla lacking smash attacks, the game feels very linear and is much more like a 2d fighter than a smash bros game. It's kinda hard to explain, but smash is more fluid while BH is more rigid, but is put in a setting (wide screen, platforms) that fits a more smash bros style of game.
Another feature Brawlhalla has are special attack bound to a certain button which change based on the direction, like smash you have an up, down and side special, but unlike smash your neutral special is the same as your up special. Also, in smash you can use all your special in the air, while in BH you can only use your up and down special, which makes the combat very linear IMO.
A mechanic that BH uses is it's 3 seperate combat systems per each character, each character can fight without an item but items are dropped during the game that yourt character has to pick up. Each character has 2 weapons they can use which are given roationally each time you pick up a weapon. For example, the character I use most has guns and guantlets, first you start with no weapon, then when you grab a weapon you'll get the guns, then if you drop the weapon and pick up another you'll get the guantlets, then the guns, guantlets, ect. This would be a good system if each character used different weapons, but sadly their are only six or so weapons between around 40 characters, meaning the only difference in characters are their weapon combinations and stats, which makes almost every character feel exactly the same. The only other difference is that different specials even if they have the same weapon, but still have the same basic attacks.
Other than the lack of variety in play styles in characters I have 2 big gameplay complaints:
1.pushing up on the joystick wont make you jump
2.camping is encouraged
Unlike other fighters where sitting still wont get you anywhere, in BH you can stand completely still and wait out your opponent with no consequences, unlike smash where characters either have projectiles to make their oppenent move, or have abilities that make them able to attack a defending oppenent and makie them have to counter attack, BH doesn't have that, in BH if you have a staff or axe you can just sit their, and if your opponent comes you just hit them away, in my first 3 matches online this is all my opponents did.
Another failed system is the character skins, each character can get new skins, weapon skins, colors and taunts, but each of these cost real money, with a character skin usually costing around 5 dollars. Yes, there is an in game currency, but the only things you can buy with those are characters, which I bought all of (after I spent 20 dollars to get them), which brings me to my next compaint, like a MOBA, only some characters are available for free and they rotate every once in a while so if you find a character you like you have to buy them, wither with real currency or in-game currency.
Overall this isn't a bad game, just a flawed one. I recommend getting an emulator and playing smash, it's free and with Netplay, you can play online. Of course I recommend Melee, as it is the best vanilla smash game, but the PM mod for Brawl is great too. And besides, Smash actually has a competitive scene people care about.

Ziggurat is a first person dungeon crawler with hectic combat, procedural levels and permadeath. You play as an apprentice sorcerer who needs to complete his final trial to graduate.
Visually Ziggurat looks like a cheap mobile title, which does not do the game any favors. The enemy designs in particular are quite boring.
The sound effects are rather poor. The music is decent but rather repetitive.
To complete your trial you need to progress through five procedurally generated levels. Each level consists of interconnected rooms, which typically contain either enemies, traps or altars. The enemy rooms have few further variations too, including special modifiers and additional goals in addition to the simple monster slaying.
Too bad the combat itself is rather lackluster. The weapons often feel weak and the enemies aren't particularly interesting. The room designs are rather repetitive too and quite annoyingly all the battles take place in small closed-off rooms.
Like many poor roguelikes, the game also suffers from overreliance on RNG. In particular you only get a very limited amount of weapons and this can make a huge difference in game diffulty.
The controls are pretty decent.
The game does not really have much writing or story.
Personally I found Ziggurat a rather lackluster game with weak combat, heavy reliance on RNG and low production values. Unless you really enjoy the FPS combat and the magic weapons, you are much better off playing the many other superior roguelikes/roguelites available on Steam.

Ziggurat is a fast-paced first-person dungeon crawler where you simply go room to room shooting baddies with various magical weapons.
Similar to Binding of Isaac, maps are procedurally generated, with a boss at the end of each floor and multiple floors in each dungeon, constituting a single "run". The idea is to play until you either die or clear all floors. Between each run, new items and unlocks are earned, which affect future playthroughs.
Ziggurat runs are on the shorter side, with 5 floors per dungeon that will take you around an hour to 90 minutes. Other game modes are available, such as an endless version, which allow for different experiences.
Ziggurat isn't terrible, but it feels lackluster as a Rogue-lite. It kept me entertained for a quick playthrough, but with the lack of impactful/meaningful upgrades during and between runs, I felt little to no progression, and thus had no reason to keep playing beyond a few runs.
It's not a particularly pretty game (PS2 level graphics), and the enemies aren't all that unique or interesting, leaving me with a stale feeling after playing for a couple of hours.
I can't exactly recommend this game when there are many stronger alternatives.

Let me start by saying that Ziggurat is hard. REALLY hard. The term "rogue-like" means that there is permadeath( you can still progress, but to "beat" Ziggurat you must make a full run-through) and procedural generation, which keeps each run-through unique by providing new dungeon layouts with each playthrough. Ziggurat, like many rogue-likes, places you in seemingly impossible scenarios with enemies all over the place. With all these enemies, it's overwhelming to know how to react at first, which is why skill is such a necessary part of playing Ziggurat.
Ziggurat may require a lot of skill, but there is one large issue that no amount of skill can protect you from: auto-tracking. Most of the enemies is Ziggurat have percect aim because they are constantly locked on to you. Even if I jump or run, enemies still hit me most of the time because they're still following me percectly when preparing to hit me, and I can deal with that to some degree, but what's worse is when the shots follow you. I can't tell you how many times I've been damaged or even killed from across the room, over a staircase and behind a wall because an enemy's shot has been following me for the past 30 seconds. This entire issue makes the easy difficulty the only viable option when playing.
I have only one other issue with Ziggurat, and that is the fact that enemies often get stuck out of bounds. This usually happens with the flying enemies, but also happens with enemies tha lunge at me. This often prevents me from gathering the drops from slain enemies and slows me down because it's really hard to hit enemis that are pressed up against a wall and under a bridge.
Ziggurat may not be perfect, but on the whole it has some good concepts and is well-polished, and that is why I rate Ziggurat as a 4 out of 5.

Okay, let's start off this review.
Ballistic overkill was overhyped by myself and many other players for the release of this early access - beta. It has three classes to choose from and a wide weapon selection from each as well as three different weapon slots to select and "Switch em up" while in game. There is so many changes from the original ballistic game we all came to love and know - but that doesn't mean the game will be changed too much for the worst.
The pros:
- Lovely visuals
- Customization of settings
- Variety of weapons
- Excellent developer support
- Balanced maps
- Ability to create your own match, open or private
The cons:
- Laggy servers
- Connectivity issues
- OP grenades
- Enemy team has the ability to kill in spawn (Even with the separate team guards)
- Matches (especially King of the hill) do not seem long enough
- No exp earned at the end of a match - Reason I put this, we're testing a game, you'd want us to be able to rank up and test out all the bugs from each rank up.
All of the cons are an easy fix through a few or several updates. As this is only early access, we can expect the game to go far in the future. I'm looking forward to the turn out of this game.

Being a big fan of Star Wars and LEGO alike, I thoroughly enjoyed my playthrough of the magnificent Saga in fantastic blocky form. As you would expect from a title like this, you will embark on a journey across the entire 6 episodes of Star Wars, following a fairly close storyline to that of the movies - just don't expect as much detail. It took me 9 hours to get through all the main levels, although I only finished about 40% of the game, so clearly there is a lot to see and do! With over 120 playable characters, 6 episodes with 6 chapters each, bonus levels, collectibles throughout all levels, and local co-op drop-in drop-out mode, what is there not to love!
Everything from character designs, classic scenes and vehicles, and sounds are just brilliant! The combat and puzzle elements are what is to be expected from a LEGO game (and if you're not familiar with them, what I mean by this is that they're nothing too special), but it's LEGO... and Star Wars... so the game has to be good! And it is!! Although I did enjoy the first 3 episodes over the Original Trilogy... sorry die-hard fans - I just found that in the game they were more interesting and less tedious.
Overall, it's a fantastic game, and it's something that anyone can get into - regardless of age or interest. May the force be with you!

Probably one of the best games i've played last gen. A lot of good games came out over the past few years, and this one certainly stands out amongst them. The first in a span of three games (although Origins is a prequel), it laid the foundation for what a Batman game could be. The combat is fluid and intuitive.. countering whenever necessary to protect yourself from foes.  However, what it does fall short on is responsiveness. There were moments where i would hit the counter button during a good time, and Batman would not counter the enemy. Frustrating, but tolerable. The game is very interactive with its gameplay mechanics.. use spray gel to blast through walls, remote controlled batarangs, the list goes on with the many gadgets Batman has in his employ. It's surely better not to spoil it for you. As much as the gadgets and power-ups fulfilled my obsessive compulsive desires for gadgets and power-ups, there were also backgrounds on each character and special collectibles to find throughout Arkham Asylum. There's a lot to learn in this game if you're a newcomer to Batman, and this game delivers for those out of the loop. The story is, in my opinion, the strongest amongst the three. Certainly a great game to pick up and have in your collection.
